notes:
Read all 5 non-original DHRL_USD workbooks plus the original EX_DATA['DHRL'] entry as Rosetta Stone. All figures cross-checked row-by-row from each workbook's 'Repayment Schedule' tab (opening/interest/principal/closing columns), converted dates to Excel serials (epoch 1899-12-30). Implied per-period rates were back-solved (interest / opening * 360/days) at multiple points in every file and matched the stated LIBOR+5% margin exactly, confirming this is a genuine 3M-LIBOR/SOFR floating facility; day_count_basis=360 holds throughout all versions. Chronological chain (5 versions produced, one per file):

1. 'DHRL_ Loan_Rescheduled_27 Jun'19.xls' -> 1st Reschedule, effective 2019-07-15 (decision date 2019-06-13). The original loan (44 qtrly installments, matures 2028-03-15) accrued 3 quarters of interest without full payment around 2019 and IDCOL capitalized USD 709,269.17 of unpaid interest into principal, converted the payment frequency from quarterly to monthly, and extended the tenor to 2030-09-15 (135 monthly installments from the new opening balance of USD 19,860,260.96). Verified: opening 19,860,260.96 -> closing 0.00 over 135 rows, constant principal amortization of 147,113.04/month.

2. 'DHRL_ Loan_Restructured.xls' (NO ordinal) -> placed as a DRAFT/ALTERNATE version of the SAME June-2019 event. Evidence: its pre-event rows (through 2019-06-13, opening 18,000,000, interest 345,492.875) are byte-identical to the other files' pre-reschedule rows, and its reschedule effective date is also 2019-06-13/2019-09-15 (same trigger event) -- but here NO interest is capitalized, the original 2028-03-15 maturity is KEPT (only 35 quarterly installments at flat 500,000/quarter principal, i.e., the original step-up schedule continued unchanged), and dates are cleanly aligned to the 15th of the quarter month (vs. the executed version's irregular monthly dates that preserve the original day-of-month drift). Because it under-delivers for the lender (no capitalization of unpaid interest, no tenor relief priced in) relative to the actually-executed 'Rescheduled 27 Jun'19' file, and because IDCOL's actual DHRL_Loan header sheet (repeated verbatim in every other workbook) explicitly records 'Interest Capitalized: 709,269.17' as a hard fact of the loan's history, I concluded this file is a SUPERSEDED DRAFT proposal for the June-2019 reschedule, not a distinct later event. I still emit it as its own version entry per instructions (every file must produce >=1 version) with eventType RESCHEDULE and a label flagging it as the superseded draft; its verification numbers are internally consistent (opening 17,500,000 -> closing 0 over 35 rows) even though it was not the path actually taken.

3. 'DHRL_ Loan_2nd Restructured_Jul'21.xls' -> 2nd Restructure, effective 2020-04-15, decided/executed by Jul-2021. This file's schedule is identical to the 1st Reschedule file through 2020-03-15, then principal payments STOP (COVID-related deferral) while interest continues to accrue and get capitalized into a rising opening balance each period from 2020-04-15 through 2021-06-15 (opening balance climbs from 18,536,243.56 to a plateau of 19,832,960.03 -- total interest capitalized during the freeze = 1,296,716.47), interest-only payments resume from 2021-07-15 (balance held flat, no further capitalization), and principal amortization resumes 2022-07-14 at a new fixed amount of 137,728.89/month, extending tenor to a new maturity of 2034-06-15. Classified MORATORIUM_EXTENSION since the defining change is principal deferral (with associated interest capitalization) rather than a rate renegotiation. Verified: opening 18,536,243.56 -> closing 0 over 171 rows.

4. 'DHRL_USD_Loan_3rd Restructured_Dec'22.xls' -> 3rd Restructure, effective 2022-07-14 (decided Dec-2022, applied retroactively to the date principal was due to resume per the 2nd Restructure). This file is identical to the 2nd Restructure file through 2022-06-15, but the principal-resumption date already reached in that file (2022-07-14) is pushed back a further 12 months to 2023-07-13 -- i.e., another interest-only moratorium year is granted, with maturity extended one more year to 2035-06-15. No additional capitalization occurs in this event itself (interest is paid current throughout, not capitalized) -- it purely defers principal and stretches tenor. Classified MORATORIUM_EXTENSION. Verified: opening 19,832,960.03 -> closing 0 over 156 rows.

5. 'DHRL_USD_Loan_3rd Restructured_Dec'22_RateChange.xls' -> modeled as a separate RATE_CHANGE version, effective 2025-12-15. This file is row-for-row IDENTICAL to the 3rd Restructured file (same principal schedule, same tenor to 2035-06-15, same capitalization/moratorium history) up through 2025-11-13; the two files diverge starting exactly at the 2025-12-15 installment, where the base 3rd-Restructured file's implied floating rate flattens to a forward-projection of 8.9832% (its last actual LIBOR/SOFR fixing held constant into the future) while the RateChange file instead flattens to 7.1722% -- an ~181bp reduction reflecting an updated (lower) benchmark projection/reset, with the fixed 5% margin unchanged in both. Since this is purely a revised floating-rate-benchmark assumption applied prospectively (no new capitalization, no principal/tenor change, no overdue roll-in), I chose to represent it as its own lightweight RATE_CHANGE version chained off the 3rd Restructure's balance at 2025-12-15 (opening 15,838,822.25) rather than folding it into the 3rd Restructure version's params, because the schema's `interest_rate_change_events` array lives inside a single version's params and is meant for rate resets WITHIN one version's own life (which I also used for the small mid-life 2026-01-15 flattening inside version 4's params) -- whereas this is a wholesale re-projection of ALL remaining periods after a fixed cutover date, cleaner to express as its own version boundary for the versioning system's audit trail. Verified: opening 15,838,822.25 -> closing 0 over 115 rows.

Cross-checks performed: (a) each version's opening balance equals the prior version's closing/rolled-forward balance at the same calendar date (18,536,243.56 matches the 1st Reschedule's balance as of 2020-03-15/04-15; 19,832,960.03 matches the 2nd Restructure's plateau balance as of 2022-07-14; 15,838,822.25 matches the 3rd Restructure's balance as of 2025-12-15); (b) implied per-period interest rates were spot-checked against the LIBOR-curve + 5% margin header rows in each workbook and matched to within rounding; (c) all row counts, first-row, and last-row values were independently verified against the raw Excel data before being embedded in the override arrays -- no values were derived by formula/assumption, every interest/principal/opening/closing figure is a direct read from the workbook's own computed schedule (all versions use override arrays for full accuracy given irregular stub periods, floating rates, and moratorium mechanics that cannot be cleanly reproduced from first-principles formulas). No waived (forgiven) amounts were found in any file -- all interest relief took the form of capitalization (into principal) or deferral (moratorium), never forgiveness, consistent with prior research. No explicit DFIM circular reference was found printed in any of these workbooks; regulatory context (BB approval, COVID-related forbearance) is inferred from the nature/timing of the 2020-2023 moratorium extensions and stated only where reasonably inferable, otherwise left null.
